title: AI/ML Engineer Academy
valueStatement: Interactive environment to design, test, and validate production AI systems end to end.
architectureHighlight: Covers accuracy contracts, agent orchestration, secure serving, evaluation, rollback, and operational governance.
description: An interactive training platform for production AI/ML: five curriculum modules, architecture simulators, isolated Python labs, and a field atlas that distinguishes CPU-proved work from survey topics.
pitch: Interactive environment to design, test, and validate production AI systems end to end.
challenge: Most AI courses skip the unglamorous half: Docker, evals, promotion gates, and the difference between a local notebook and a served system. The academy had to train that stack without pretending a browser quiz is production competence.
development: Built a React 19 + Vite 6 SPA with an Express server, optional Grok mentor, and five isolated lab virtualenvs (dependencies conflict across modules on purpose). Curriculum maps SWE+ML, transformers/MoE/LoRA, RAG/MCP/LangGraph, system design, and cloud productionization. A standalone static atlas page states who it is for and which topics are CPU-proved vs survey.
outcome: A private training applet with local certificate unlock (modules + lab evidence + quiz threshold). Not a vendor credential. Interactive app needs Node; this static portfolio cannot host it. Source: github.com/rubyrayjuntos/AIML-Engineer-Academy.

gallery.title: Learning control plane
gallery.description: Holographic model, code, retrieval, security, and evals around one engineer — the academy’s metaphor for putting the whole stack in one field of view

journey.title: Train the job, not the buzzword
journey.description: Started from the skill matrix: SWE+ML, LLM internals, orchestration, system design, deployment. If it is not on that matrix, it is not a module.

journey.title: Labs that conflict on purpose
journey.description: Each module gets its own venv. CUDA, vector drivers, and classical ML stacks do not belong in one requirements.txt — engineers learn that the hard way, which is the point.

journey.title: Evidence before the keepsake
journey.description: Certificate unlock requires completed modules, confirmed lab evidence, and a quiz bar. The PDF in localStorage is a souvenir, not an accredited credential.

journey.title: Atlas as the honest map
journey.description: A static field atlas separates CPU-proved labs from survey and optional-live topics so the marketing page cannot outrun the work.

specs.title: Five-module production curriculum
specs.description: Foundations (Python, Docker, classical ML), LLM architectures (attention, DPO/GRPO, MoE, LoRA/QLoRA), agent orchestration (RAG, MCP, DSPy, LangGraph), system design, cloud productionization.

specs.title: Isolated labs with pytest evidence
specs.description: module-1 through module-5 each ship requirements.txt and validation commands. Passing tests is the evidence object, not a checked box in the UI.

specs.title: Mentor in the loop, curriculum without it
specs.description: Optional xAI Grok mentor behind XAI_API_KEY. The applet still teaches if the key is missing — same pattern as Kitchen Kontrol’s Gemini assistant.

specs.title: Field atlas, not a sales page
specs.description: Standalone static atlas: audience, contents, non-goals, and a filterable map of proved vs survey topics. Shared learning-space pitch.

specs.title: This site cannot host the applet
specs.description: SPA + Express on port 3000. Portfolio is static HTML. Host later via Pages/Render; until then the case study and GitHub are the public surface.
